key_insight: The paper reconstructs molten-pool surface flow fields from high-speed video by combining optical-flow measurements with physics-informed neural networks that enforce fluid dynamics constraints.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable, physically grounded monitoring of wire-arc DED melt-pool behavior, which can improve bead geometry control, defect prevention, and microstructure consistency.
method: Homography-corrected high-speed images are converted into dense optical-flow velocity observations.
A PINN reconstructs quasi-steady surface flow by minimizing data error plus incompressible Navier–Stokes and no-penetration boundary losses.
For droplet-impact cases, a phase-conditioned time-dependent PINN captures cyclic flow evolution over the impact period.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation on high-speed video from a GTAW-based wire-arc DED process under two regimes: quasi-steady convection and periodic droplet impact.
watch_item: Accuracy may depend on camera calibration, optical-flow quality, and how well the assumed 2D surface-flow and boundary-condition priors match the real melt pool.
paper_title: Reconstruction of Molten Pool Flow Fields from High-Speed Video Using Physics-Informed Neural Networks
